ownership.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
ownership.confidence_note: No legal entity, founders, team page, or 'About' page could be found; the marketing site itself (per the research card's caveats) closely mirrors Steel.dev's blog structure and personas, and docs.ferr.dev / GitHub / PyPI / Docker endpoints referenced on the site do not resolve. Treat 'independent' as a weak default, not a confirmed corporate fact.

stage.note: No press release, Crunchbase/PitchBook profile, YC page, or company statement about any funding round was found. ycombinator.com/companies/ferr returns 404, crunchbase.com/organization/ferr returns 403 (no confirmable public profile), and web searches for "ferr.dev" funding/seed return only unrelated medical (Ferritin blood test), Ferrari, and stock-photo ('Ferr-Art') results — no company matches. Combined with the research card's own caveat that ferr.dev appears to be a clone/rebrand of Steel.dev's marketing site with non-functioning docs/app/GitHub/PyPI/Docker endpoints, there is no evidence this is an operating, fundable company at all.

note: No corporate, funding, or team information could be found beyond the marketing site itself. Per the provider card's own caveats, ferr.dev's content (blog slugs, author personas, 'stealth mode', pricing structure) closely parallels Steel.dev with 'steel' replaced by 'ferr' ('ferrum' = Latin for iron/steel), and the product's own referenced endpoints (docs.ferr.dev, the app, GitHub repo, PyPI package, Docker image) do not resolve/exist. Treat this as an unverifiable or possibly non-operational marketing site rather than a real funded company; all funding/revenue/backer fields are unknown.
